visuals.title: What CN VII reaches
visuals.text: The facial nerve leaves the brainstem, runs through the facial canal by the ear, and supplies face muscles, tear glands, stapedius and taste.

glossary.Palsy: Paralysis or weakness of a muscle or group of muscles.
glossary.Viral reactivation: A dormant virus in nerve cells becoming active again.
glossary.Diabetes: Condition of raised blood glucose from lack of or resistance to insulin.
glossary.Facial droop: Sagging of one side of the face from muscle weakness.
glossary.Anterior 2/3 of the tongue: The front part of the tongue, whose taste is carried by the chorda tympani branch of CN VII.
glossary.Excess tearing: Watering eye, often because tears no longer drain properly as the lid is weak.
glossary.Dry mouth: Reduced saliva, from involvement of CN VII fibres to the salivary glands.
glossary.Cornea: The clear front window of the eye.
glossary.Evaporation: Loss of the tear film to the air when the eye stays open.
glossary.Stroke: Sudden brain damage from blocked or bleeding blood vessels.
glossary.Central cause: A cause inside the brain or brainstem rather than in the nerve itself.
glossary.Red flags: Features that suggest a serious alternative cause needing urgent action.
glossary.Limb weakness: Weakness in an arm or leg, pointing to a central lesion.
glossary.Cranial nerves: The 12 pairs of nerves arising directly from the brain and brainstem.
glossary.Clinical diagnosis: A diagnosis made from history and examination without needing tests.
glossary.Atypical features: Findings that do not fit the usual pattern, e.g. bilateral weakness or slow progression.
glossary.Structural cause: A physical lesion, such as a tumour, pressing on the nerve.
glossary.Complete facial paralysis: Total loss of movement on one side of the face.
glossary.Artificial tears: Lubricating eye drops that replace the natural tear film.
glossary.Eye ointment: Thick lubricant applied to the eye, usually at night.
glossary.Referral: Sending a patient to a specialist team.
glossary.Bony facial canal: The narrow channel in the temporal bone through which the facial nerve runs.
glossary.Compression: Squeezing of the nerve, here by swelling inside a tight canal.
glossary.Cortical innervation: Nerve supply coming from the cerebral cortex.
glossary.Spontaneous resolution: Getting better on its own without treatment.
glossary.Steroids: Anti-inflammatory drugs, here prednisolone, that reduce nerve swelling.
glossary.Temporal bone: Skull bone at the side of the head containing the middle and inner ear.
glossary.Greater petrosal nerve: Branch of CN VII supplying the tear (lacrimal) gland.
glossary.Lacrimal gland: Gland above the outer eye that makes tears.
